decisions.reason: The firm has sunk tooling and mould costs into this niche agricultural crate and it was still mentioned in 2019, so management will likely attribute any weak sales to temporary pandemic and harvest-market disruptions rather than drop it.

The foldable large container had a dedicated page in both years, which signals strong public commitment and centrality to the firm's returnable-packaging direction, so management is strongly inclined to persist.
The stackable crate sits at the core of the firm's established crate business, and with mould investments already sunk, keeping it is the natural course.
The rackable pallet fits the firm's pallet range and has been visibly presented since 2018, so disappointing results would be attributed to temporary supply-chain and raw-material shocks.
It moved from a dedicated page to a mere mention, which suggests reduced emphasis, but the sunk investment and the earlier public commitment likely sustain it for another year.
It was downgraded from its own page to a mention, but the pallet is a variant of the core pallet line with mould costs already incurred, so management will likely justify keeping it.
